findings.rationale: D3 names a live trusted-cwd caller-boundary repair without explicitly binding it to the named backlog entry; the frozen plan must make that identity and scope relationship explicit before implementation.
The plan currently places doc-sync and backlog removal after integration; the reviewed cumulative candidate must own those mutations before its final freeze.
D6's stated performance acceptance lacks an executable benchmark contract and validator, so it cannot be mechanically closed as written.
The final authority wording does not bind verifier/reviewer identity and every repaired candidate to exact base and candidate SHAs; this is an immediate integrity gap.
The integrated review ledger and fail-closed transport/generation accounting are not explicit enough to prevent a hidden retry or generation escape.
D1-D7, D4 live trials, final seats, repairs, and D8 retries lack exact pre-spend reservations and a bound terminal evidence receipt.
The plan's 32 conditional-entry count is stale against the current canonical backlog count of 29 and must be reconciled before review can authorize execution.
The listed completion commands do not mechanically prove authorization, exact backlog removal, review provenance, integration ancestry, or archival terminal state.
D7 and D8 leave decision thresholds and experiment policy choices open while declaring no open questions; those rules must be frozen before admission.
